<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

PRD 006 compiled the ten type definitions and seeds into the daemon (`templates/types/<type>/v<N>/`). A hand-written page per type would be a second copy, so the type pages are rendered from the catalog when pij-rs runs: always the binary's own types. Pages are now file pages (any repository file, so the skill's concepts page is bundled rather than copied) or generated pages; each carries its sources as compiled in. `docs get --json` returns them (a file's text, or a parsed document), and plan 239's check compares text byte for byte and documents as parsed JSON, so an edited type definition fails `harness checks` until pij-rs is rebuilt.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A seat in any repo reads what a seat, role, type, position, pod, seed and template are, and every type's definition, from pij.
- One copy of each page: the skill's concepts page and the type catalog are the sources, never duplicated.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- The pods page: it waits on workstream 008 step s02.
- Refusals and first turns naming pages (step s04, after workstream 007 step s02).
- A repo's own seeds in the type pages: those are governance (`pij directory types <type> --seed`), which docs never reads.

<a id="research-context"></a>

## Research Context

Blueprint 005 c-type-catalog (`crates/daemon/src/community/types.rs`) compiles each `type.dd.json` and `seed.md` with `include_bytes!`/`include_str!` and parses them once (`all()`); `TypeDef` keeps the parsed `document` and the `seed` text, so a page can carry both as sources without a file read. Blueprint 005 c-docs names the concepts page in `skills/pij/references/community/`; pm-001 assigned it to this step so it has one writer.

<a id="risks"></a>

## Risks

| risk | likelihood | impact | mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A new type version ships and a page still names the old path. | Low | Low | Paths come from each TypeDef's version, and the check compares the file at that path. |

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Cost: no loop, poll, timer, hook or launch. Pages are rendered in-process from bytes already in the binary, once per call; nothing reads governance or contacts the daemon. The check adds one `docs get` per new page (fourteen in all) inside `harness checks` only.
- Pages are public-safe: no customer or person names.
